# kenze

> Big-file data prep that never runs out of memory — an interactive shell and a one-line CLI, powered by DuckDB. kenze cleans and reshapes data files (CSV, Parquet, JSON) that are too big for pandas, streaming everything out-of-core so a file larger than RAM never raises MemoryError. No SQL required.

kenze is a Python tool (`pip install kenze`) for people who hit `MemoryError` in pandas on a large CSV/Parquet/JSON file. It is a friendly front-end over DuckDB: DuckDB does the streaming, disk-spill, and multi-core work; kenze auto-configures memory so the job does not crash, and exposes simple verbs (no SQL) both as an interactive shell and a one-line CLI.

## What it solves
- Reading and processing a CSV/Parquet file that is larger than RAM without crashing (out-of-core / larger-than-memory data prep).
- Cleaning, filtering, deduping, joining, reshaping, and ML-prep on big files with no SQL and no pandas out-of-memory errors.
- A friendly alternative to writing DuckDB SQL by hand, and to pandas for files too big for memory.

## Key facts
- Install: `pip install kenze` — one name for the package, the `kenze` command, and `import kenze`.
- Interactive shell: run `kenze` with no args for a live session (load once, stack steps with live previews, run to a file or save a recipe). Type `/` for a command menu; TAB autocompletes real column names.
- One-line CLI: 38 commands — keep, drop, filter, rename, cast, fillna, dedup, sample, join, diff, pivot, split, partition, and more.
- Model-ready: scale, bin, encode, onehot, clip-outliers, and a reproducible traintest split for scikit-learn / XGBoost.
- Never-OOM: memory is auto-capped and DuckDB spills to disk; full writes stream with a progress bar.
- Formats: CSV, Parquet, JSON, Excel (.xlsx), plus s3:// / gs:// / https:// cloud paths.
